title: Homotopy lifting for maps from a CW complex
statement: Use path components and continuous based homotopy groups as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A CW complex is a space constructed from the empty space by attaching a set of closed $n$-disks along their boundary spheres to the $(n-1)$-skeleton, for each integer $n\geq0$, with the weak topology for its characteristic disk maps and with each cell boundary contained in finitely many lower-dimensional cells. Let $K$ be a CW complex, let $A,B$ be arbitrary topological spaces, and let $w:A\to B$ be continuous, inducing a bijection on path components and group isomorphisms $\pi_n(A,a)\to\pi_n(B,w(a))$ for every $a\in A$ and $n\geq1$. For each continuous $u:K\to B$, there exist a continuous $v:K\to A$ and a continuous $H:K\times[0,1]\to B$ with $H(k,0)=w(v(k))$ and $H(k,1)=u(k)$. No CW hypothesis on $A$ or $B$, connectedness hypothesis, or fixed-basepoint condition is imposed; empty spaces are allowed.

source.place: Kerodon Lemma 3.6.3.11 (Tag 0140): lifting maps with CW source through an arbitrary weak homotopy equivalence up to homotopy. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. This is a Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag. Weak-equivalence hypotheses expanded using Remark 3.6.3.4 in Kerodon Subsection 3.6.3.

proof.text: Fix the cell structure of $K$ from the statement and write $K_{-1}=\varnothing$ and $K_n$ for its $n$-skeleton. We construct, by induction on $n\geq-1$, continuous maps $v_n:K_n\to A$ and $H_n:K_n\times I\to B$, where $I=[0,1]$, such that $H_n(k,0)=w(v_n(k))$, $H_n(k,1)=u(k)$, and both maps restrict exactly to their predecessors. The maps with empty domain give the base case $n=-1$, with all equalities vacuous.

source.place: Lemma 3.6.3.11 (Kerodon 0140), proof by recursion on the skeleta; agent expansion of the quotient-continuity details.

proof.text: Assume $(v_{n-1},H_{n-1})$ has been constructed. For each $n$-cell $e$, let $\chi_e:D^n\to K_n$ be its characteristic map and $b_e:S^{n-1}\to K_{n-1}$ its boundary map. Define $\alpha_e=v_{n-1}b_e$, $\beta_e=u\chi_e$ and $h_e(s,t)=H_{n-1}(b_e(s),t)$. They are continuous, and the inductive endpoint identities give $h_e(s,0)=w(\alpha_e(s))$ and $h_e(s,1)=\beta_e|_{S^{n-1}}(s)$ because $\chi_e|_{S^{n-1}}=b_e$. Apply [lem-cbc-weak-equivalence-relative-disk-extension] with this $w$, this dimension $n$, and these three maps. Its component and based-group hypotheses are exactly the hypotheses on $w$ in the item. Choose the resulting maps $a_e:D^n\to A$ and $G_e:D^n\times I\to B$. In dimension zero the boundary data are empty and the same lemma still applies; no source basepoint or connectedness is needed.

source.place: Lemma 3.6.3.11 (Kerodon 0140), proof by recursion on the skeleta; agent expansion of the quotient-continuity details.

proof.text: The attaching construction makes $q_n:K_{n-1}\amalg\coprod_eD^n\to K_n$ a quotient map. Put $v_{n-1}$ and $a_e$ on its summands. They agree at every boundary identification since $a_e|_{S^{n-1}}=v_{n-1}b_e$, so descend to a function $v_n$. It is continuous: for an open $U\subseteq A$, $q_n^{-1}(v_n^{-1}(U))$ is open on each summand, hence open in the coproduct, and the quotient criterion gives that $v_n^{-1}(U)$ is open. Similarly $H_{n-1}$ and the $G_e$ descend to a function $H_n:K_n\times I\to B$, since $G_e(s,t)=H_{n-1}(b_e(s),t)$ for every boundary point and every $t$. Its pullback along $q_n\times\operatorname{id}_I$ is continuous: the product of a topological coproduct with $I$ has the corresponding open summands, and each restriction is one of the continuous maps just specified. Apply [lem-cbc-quotient-cylinder-continuity] to $q_n$, $T=I$ and $Z=B$. The interval is locally compact (small closed subinterval neighborhoods form a compact neighborhood basis, with one-sided intervals at its endpoints). Thus $H_n$ is continuous for the ordinary product topology. All endpoint identities and both predecessor restrictions hold on every summand, hence everywhere by surjectivity of $q_n$. This completes the inductive step.

source.place: Lemma 3.6.3.11 (Kerodon 0140), proof by recursion on the skeleta; agent expansion of the quotient-continuity details.

proof.text: Induction and choice over the sets of cells produce one compatible sequence $(v_n,H_n)$. Since $K=\bigcup_{n\geq0}K_n$, set $v(k)=v_n(k)$ and $H(k,t)=H_n(k,t)$ for any $n$ with $k\in K_n$. These definitions are independent of $n$ by exact compatibility. For every cell $e$ of dimension $n$, we have $v\chi_e=a_e$ and $H(\chi_e(x),t)=G_e(x,t)$, including boundary points, because later stages restrict to stage $n$.

source.place: Lemma 3.6.3.11 (Kerodon 0140), proof by recursion on the skeleta; agent expansion of the quotient-continuity details.

proof.text: Let $q:\coprod_{n\geq0}\coprod_{e\text{ an }n\text{-cell}}D^n\to K$ be the coproduct of all characteristic maps. These maps cover $K$, and the weak-topology clause in the definition of the CW structure says precisely that $q$ is a quotient map. Each restriction of $v q$ is the continuous map $a_e$, so the same inverse-open-set argument as in step 3 proves $v$ continuous. Each restriction of $(x,t)\mapsto H(q(x),t)$ is the continuous $G_e$, so the product-coproduct observation in step 3 proves this pullback continuous. Apply [lem-cbc-quotient-cylinder-continuity] again, now to $q$ and $T=I$, to obtain continuity of $H$ on the ordinary product $K\times I$. The endpoint identities follow on every $K_n$ and hence on $K$: $H(k,0)=w(v(k))$ and $H(k,1)=u(k)$. If $K$ is empty the empty maps already give the conclusion. The construction imposed no CW structure on $A$ or $B$ and no basepoint condition.
